question.text: Per the SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/AFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/123 dated September 19, 2024 on modification in framework for valuation, an independent valuer engaged by a Cat I/II AIF that is a partnership entity or company must be:

answer.text: A Chartered Accountant firm with minimum 5 years experience
A Registered Valuer Entity registered with IBBI, with the deputed person(s) holding membership of ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI or CFA Charter
An investment bank empanelled with SEBI
Any credit rating agency's subsidiary without any further requirement

explanation.text: The Logic: The Sep 19, 2024 SEBI Circular (footnote 123 in the PDF) tightened the eligibility: for partnership/company valuers, the ENTITY must be a Registered Valuer Entity (RVE) registered with IBBI, AND the deputed/authorised person actually performing the valuation must hold ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI membership or a CFA Charter. This replaced the prior looser criteria. The Trap: CA firm with 5 years experience was the earlier norm before the amendment; investment bank empanelment is not a SEBI requirement; standalone CRA subsidiary now requires additional certification. The 2024 amendment was specifically about tightening both entity and individual eligibility. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same 2024 amendment. XIX-D is the first exam cycle tested post-Sep 2024 — expect fresh questions on this. IBBI Registered Valuer rules derive from Companies Act 2013 Section 247.
